subject: AWS listing: product brief + trial entitlement / SKU visibility

From: Elise Wong <elise.wong@acmeanalytics.com>

Cc: ProductOps <marketplace@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS listing: product brief + trial entitlements / SKU visibility

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. We're moving toward our AWS Marketplace listing and need help aligning the product-facing brief (hero + bullets) and how trial entitlements will map to AMI/SKU visibility. Two specific asks:

1) Can you draft a short hero line (1 sentence) + 3 benefit bullets tuned for marketplace buyers? We want something concise for the top of the product page.

2) We need confirmation on how trial SKUs show up in the listing: can trial be an entitlement that displays a "Try free" CTA for a 14-day trial, and which SKU IDs must be present to make trial discoverable? Attached is our sample SKU sheet (acme_sku_sample.csv) and our one-pager.

Target timeline: publish draft to Seller Console by Tuesday (May 11) and request AWS PM review the next day.

Elise
Product Manager, Acme Analytics
acmeanalytics.com

Attachments: acme_sku_sample.csv (CSV), acme_product_onepager.pdf (PDF)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elise Wong <elise.wong@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: ProductOps <marketplace@acmeanalytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing: product brief + trial entitlements / SKU visibility

Hi Elise — thanks for the sheet and timeline. Drafted a compact hero + bullets below (first pass) and a proposed SKU->entitlement mapping in the attached CSV (sku_mapping_proposal.csv). Please review and flag any AMI/SKU IDs that must remain as-is.

DRAFT HERO (single line)
Redwood Inference for Acme Analytics — production-grade model inference with predictable cost and enterprise controls.

3 BENEFITS
• Predictable production performance: dedicated GPU-backed endpoints and transparent latency SLOs for real-time analytics.
• Security and control: VPC/private deployment options plus audit logs and KMS integration for regulated data.
• Cost-aware scaling: intelligent batching and reserved capacity to keep inference costs predictable as usage grows.

SKU / ENTITLEMENT NOTES (summary)
• Trial SKU suggestion: ACME-TRIAL-14D — maps to a 14-day trial entitlement which should surface the "Try free" CTA.
• Paid SKU examples: ACME-BASIC, ACME-PRO — appear as purchasable SKUs.
• Visibility: AWS shows trial CTA when a marketplace product has a trial entitlement tied to a public SKU. I attached a proposed mapping — please confirm the exact AMI/Seller SKU IDs you want used.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm or edit the hero/bullets and validate AMI/SKU IDs in acme_sku_sample.csv.
2) Kimberly / Legal to sign off on the hero claims and any compliance/footnote language.
3) We push the Seller Console draft by EOD May 11, then loop in AWS PM for marketplace review.

I've attached sku_mapping_proposal.csv.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sku_mapping_proposal.csv (CSV)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing: product brief + trial entitlements / SKU visibility

Aditya — nice draft. A couple of quick edit suggestions and a legal/claims check request. Inline: 

> DRAFT HERO (single line)
> Redwood Inference for Acme Analytics — production-grade model inference with predictable cost and enterprise controls.

I prefer tightening to: "Redwood Inference + Acme Analytics — reliable, low-latency model inference for production ML at scale." Shorter and buyer-focused.

Bullets: add an explicit line about "streaming & tool-calling support" since Acme sells real-time pipelines. Suggested bullets:
• Low-latency production inference: guaranteed scoped latency SLOs and burst capacity for peak loads.
• Enterprise controls and security: VPC/private deployment, audit logs, and KMS integrations.
• Cost-optimization tools: batching, KV caching, and reserved capacity to lower per-token cost.

Legal note (Olga) — we should avoid any hard percentile claims ("40% lower cost") unless Acme has validated numbers. Also confirm the "SLA-backed" phrasing is acceptable for this listing.

Jonas — can you validate the AMI visibility behavior? My recollection: AWS surfaces trial CTA only if the trial SKU is marked public and linked to the product entitlement; also marketplace often requires a mapping file for AMI->Seller SKU so trial enrollments can be provisioned. If you can confirm by EOD we can lock the mapping.

Kimberly
Director, GTM Operations, Redwood Inference

On May 9, 2028 at 11:03 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing: product brief + trial entitlements / SKU visibility

Thanks — legal checks:

1) Remove any absolute performance or cost reduction claims unless Acme provides supporting benchmark docs. Suggested fallback language: "optimized for low latency and cost-efficient inference".
2) SLA wording: we can say "SLA-backed options available" rather than implying all customers get an SLA.
3) Evidence: if we reference "audit logs" or "KMS integration" we should have the specific KMS provider and a short note on where to find compliance artifacts. Elise — can you share a short doc (or point to the Drive link) that states which KMS vendor you plan to integrate?

Also adding a recommended asset: a brief compliance call script for AWS reviewers — I can draft.

Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Aditya / Kimberly / Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround and the guidance. A few updates from our side: 

• We're fine with Kimberly's tightened hero line, please use it.
• Compliance: we will not make hard cost claims — updated one-pager is in the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/example-acme-onepager). KMS will be AWS KMS (we use a customer-managed key).
• SKU confirmation: please use ACME-TRIAL-14D for trial, ACME-BASIC and ACME-PRO for paid tiers. Our Seller SKU/AMI mapping is included in the attached updated CSV (acme_sku_sample.csv).

Next steps:
1) Aditya — please push the draft to Seller Console by EOD May 11 (you mentioned EOD; this afternoon would be ideal).
2) Kimberly/Olga — once it's in Seller Console, please do a quick legal/govt compliance QA before we hit submit to AWS PM.
3) AWS PM — Elise, could you confirm whether the trial CTA will be immediately visible to buyers after we publish the mapping? If there is an AWS-side review window, please advise.

We attached the updated acme_sku_sample.csv with the final SKU IDs.

Thanks all — excited to get this live.

Elise Wong
Product Manager, Acme Analytics
